$comment: U58 -- the two TJA1051 transceivers get the VIO bypass capacitor they were
missing. Review item 14, the last board item on the pre-fab list.
THE FINDING, RE-MEASURED. VIO (pin 5 on both parts -- confirmed by FUNCTION,
not pin number: pin 3 is /+5V = VCC and pin 5 is /+3V3 = VIO, which is the
TJA1051T/3 pinout) had no bypass anywhere near it:
U8.5 -> nearest /+3V3 cap  C7   22.891 mm
U9.5 -> nearest /+3V3 cap  C35  26.299 mm
while VCC on the SAME two parts is decoupled at 4.252 mm by C59 and C60. That
contrast is the tell -- VIO was missed, not traded away. And /+3V3 is routed
as tracks with no pour anywhere on the board (review item 13), so there is no
plane capacitance quietly covering for it.
THE PART COSTS NOTHING TO ADD. C14663 (YAGEO CC0603KRX7R9BB104, 100nF 0603,
JLCPCB Basic) is already fitted 41 times here, so this is two more of a reel
that is already on the order: no new BOM line, no new LCSC part, no library
import, no 3D model to backfill. The schematic symbols were cloned from C59
so every supplier field is inherited rather than retyped.
GND COSTS NOTHING EITHER. /GND is poured on the Top layer across the whole
board and both sites sit inside the fill, so each cap's pad 2 lands straight
on the pour through a thermal -- no via and no track on the return path,
which is the half of a bypass loop that actually matters.
C73 (U9) IS THE EASY ONE. West of U9 is open, and /+3V3 already runs east
along y=127.333 into the pin, so the cap sits 2.36 mm away at (110.400,
128.583) with pad 1 facing north and a 0.55 mm stub up onto that track.
C72 (U8) IS NOT, AND THE REASON IS ONE DIAGONAL. /CAN1_H runs from
separates U8.5 from every open pocket north of the part. P1's courtyard
closes the west (the P1-to-U8 gap is 0.677 mm, against a 2.790 mm 0603
courtyard), U8's own body closes the south and east. A search over 4 rotations
and ~37,000 positions found the nearest spot with a clean Top-only route to be
7.08 mm away -- i.e. giving up half the benefit to avoid a layer change.
So C72 sits where it belongs, 3.51 mm from the pin, and its /+3V3 feed hops
to Bottom to pass under the diagonal:
Both vias were placed against measured windows, not by eye. Via B is the
constrained one: it must clear the /CAN1_H diagonal above it AND the
/CAN1_RX Bottom run at y=128.023 below it -- and /CAN1_RX passes 0.072 mm
from the pin's own y, which is why a Bottom approach straight to the pad is
impossible. At x=182.4 that window is 0.14 mm tall; at x=181.0 it opens to
1.54 mm, so via B goes west into the P1/U8 gap where only a via fits. It
clears the diagonal by 1.057 mm and /CAN1_RX by 1.323 mm.
The final Top segment does NOT cross the diagonal: x - y is 54.300 at via B
and 54.305 at the pin, both below 55.794, and x - y varies linearly along a
straight segment -- so the whole run stays on the pin's side.
Two vias in a bypass feed are not free, but they are ~2 nH against the ~20 nH
of the 22.9 mm track this replaces, and the return path takes none of them.
SCHEMATIC AND BOARD ARE APPLIED BY HAND, BOTH SIDES -- the route CLAUDE.md
documents for changes KiCad gives no CLI for. The symbols, wires and labels
are in the .kicad_sch (netlist verified: C72.1/C73.1 on /+3V3, C72.2/C73.2 on
/GND); the footprints and pad nets are here. place_parts REFUSES to invent
a net, so it can only ever place a part onto nets that already exist --
--schematic-parity is what proves the two halves agree.
This is NOT a KTD12 sync and does not replace one. Nothing here reconciles
the two files; they are edited to match, and then checked.

steps.step: 1/2  place both bypass caps onto the existing /+3V3 and /GND nets
2/2  feed each pad 1; both GND pads take the Top pour by thermal
